The test image shows a split/opened soybean stem with:
- Dark black sclerotia (hard fungal bodies) inside the stem
- White cottony mycelium visible along the stem tissue
- Bleached/tan dead stem tissue
- The stem appears split open revealing internal structures

This is highly characteristic of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot) — the black sclerotia inside a bleached stem with white mycelium are the classic diagnostic features. Let me verify with reference images.
Strong match — bleached stem with black sclerotia visible. Let me check more references from other classes to fulfill the budget requirement.
Charcoal rot shows tiny microsclerotia (small dots) — different from the large distinct black sclerotia in the test image. Let me check more classes.
Brown Stem Rot shows brown internal discoloration — no black sclerotia. Let me check a few more classes.

I've now used all 16 reference image views. The evidence is clear:

**Test image analysis:**
- Split/opened soybean stem
- Large, distinct black sclerotia (hard fungal bodies) inside the cavity
- White cottony mycelium along the stem
- Bleached/tan dead stem tissue

**Key comparisons:**
- **White Mold** (ref 133): Bleached stem with black sclerotia on outside — matches well
- **Charcoal Rot** (ref 116): Tiny microsclerotia under microscope — very different scale/appearance
- **Brown Stem Rot** (ref 103): Brown internal discoloration, no sclerotia
- All leaf-disease classes (Frogeye, Bacterial Blight, Cercospora, Downy Mildew, Rust): Leaf symptoms, no relevance
- Stem diseases (Fusarium, Phytophthora, SDS): External wilting, no sclerotia

The large black sclerotia + white mycelium inside a bleached stem is the pathognomonic sign of **White Mold** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*). No other class comes close visually.
